_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Brunei covering early Hindu-Buddhist settlements, Srivijaya/Majapahit influence, conversion to Islam (14th century), Brunei Sultanate golden age (15th-16th century, controlled most of Borneo and Philippines), European contact (Magellan, Spanish, Portuguese), cession of Sarawak to James Brooke (1841), British residency, Japanese occupation, oil discovery, independence 1984, and Hassanal Bolkiah's modern Brunei.

country_profile.currency: Brunei dollar (BND, pegged to Singapore dollar)

religion.note: Official state ideology: Melayu Islam Beraja (MIB — Malay Islamic Monarchy); Sharia Penal Code implemented 2014/2019

ethnic_groups.name: Malay
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant; Brunei Malay (Melayu Brunei); seven constituent groups recognised in constitution: Belait, Bisaya, Brunei, Dusun, Kedayan, Murut, Tutong

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese
ethnic_groups.notes: Hokkien, Hakka, Cantonese; long-standing trading community; some are permanent residents not citizens; commercial sector

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous (Iban, Dusun, Murut, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Iban inland; Dusun and Murut in Temburong; Penan semi-nomadic; Bisaya; some still practice traditional religions

ethnic_groups.name: Indian/South Asian
ethnic_groups.notes: Tamil, Punjabi; professional and labour sectors

ethnic_groups.name: Other (expat workers)
ethnic_groups.notes: Large foreign workforce: Filipino, Indonesian, Thai, Bangladeshi; oil/gas and domestic workers

country_profile.notes_unique: One of the wealthiest nations; no personal income tax; free education and healthcare; Sultan's palace (Istana Nurul Iman) is world's largest residential palace; two non-contiguous parts separated by Sarawak
country_profile.national_motto: Always render service with God's guidance
country_profile.national_anthem: Allah Peliharakan Sultan (God Bless the Sultan)

geography.terrain: Flat coastal plain rising to mountains in east; 70%+ primary rainforest
geography.notes: Two non-contiguous parts on Borneo's north coast (separated by Limbang, Sarawak); 70%+ virgin rainforest preserved; Temburong National Park pristine.

economy_extended.notes: Oil and gas ~60% of GDP and 90%+ of government revenue; no income tax or personal tax; Brunei Investment Agency (sovereign wealth, est $30-40B); Wawasan Brunei 2035 diversification plan; halal industry hub ambitions.

health.notes: Free healthcare for citizens; small population enables good coverage; specialist referrals to Singapore/Malaysia; diabetes prevalence high; Royal Brunei Healthcare ambitious expansion.

food_agriculture.notes: Extremely dependent on food imports; rice self-sufficiency only 4%; halal food hub ambitions; aquaculture growing; royal family owns large farms; Brunei Halal brand development.

energy.notes: 3rd largest oil producer in SE Asia; Brunei Shell Petroleum (50/50 JV); Brunei LNG plant (Japan's first LNG supplier since 1972); Champion field; Hengyi petrochemical complex (Chinese JV); reserves declining.

transport.notes: Temburong Bridge (2020, 30 km) connects the two parts of Brunei; high car ownership; no railway; Muara Port main seaport; compact size — short travel times.

tourism.notes: Low-key tourism sector; Kampong Ayer (world's largest water village); pristine rainforest ecotourism in Temburong; halal tourism growing; deterrent: alcohol ban, strict Sharia law.

legal_system.suffrage: 18 years, village elections only (no national elections)
legal_traditions: Islamic law (Sharia Penal Code, full implementation 2019)
legal_system.notes: Absolute monarchy (no elections since 1962); Sharia Penal Code implemented 2014-2019 (includes stoning for adultery, amputation for theft — moratorium on enforcement after international backlash); Sultan rules by decree.

human_rights_gender.notes: Absolute monarchy limits political rights; no elected legislature; Malay Muslim Monarchy (MIB) state ideology; Sharia Penal Code drew international criticism; media heavily controlled; women well-represented in education/some professions.

security_stability.notes: One of the world's most peaceful and secure countries; no significant crime; small population; oil wealth enables social stability; Five Power Defence Arrangements (UK, Australia, NZ, Malaysia, Singapore) member.

cultural_heritage.notes: Malay Muslim Monarchy (MIB) state philosophy; Kampong Ayer water village oldest continuously inhabited (1,000+ years); Sultan's palace (Istana Nurul Iman) largest residential palace in the world (1,788 rooms).

comparative_rankings.notes: High HDI and per-capita income; peace rankings among best globally; authoritarian governance limits freedom scores.
comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Hassanal Bolkiah
current_leader.title: Sultan and Yang di-Pertuan
current_leader.notes: 29th Sultan of Brunei; one of world's longest-reigning monarchs (57+ years); also PM, Defence and Finance Minister; one of world's wealthiest individuals; led to independence from UK 1984

crown_prince.name: Al-Muhtadee Billah
crown_prince.title: Crown Prince and Senior Minister
crown_prince.notes: Heir apparent; plays increasing governmental role

former_sultans.name: Omar Ali Saifuddien III
former_sultans.notes: 'Architect of Modern Brunei'; built Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque; rejected joining Malaysia 1963; abdicated in favour of son but remained influential until death 1986

former_sultans.name: Sultan Muhammad Shah (Awang Alak Betatar)
former_sultans.notes: First Muslim sultan; converted from Hindu-Buddhist; established Islamic dynasty; Chinese records mention Brunei tribute
